questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Anatomically, the pituitary gland is divided into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. The adenohypophysis consists of which two portions?

solution.explanation: The adenohypophysis consists of two portions, the pars distalis and the pars intermedia. The neurohypophysis is the pars nervosa (posterior pituitary).
solution.why_others_wrong: The pars nervosa is the neurohypophysis, not a part of the adenohypophysis; the hypothalamus is part of the brain, not of the pituitary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Pars distalis and pars intermedia

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An endocrine gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues; each follicle consists of follicular cells enclosing a cavity, and iodine is essential for the normal rate of its hormone synthesis. The gland is the:

solution.explanation: The thyroid gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues. Each thyroid follicle is made of follicular cells enclosing a cavity; these cells synthesise thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Iodine is essential for the normal rate of thyroid hormone synthesis.
steps: Follicles of follicular cells around a cavity
solution.why_others_wrong: None of the other glands is built of follicles around a cavity or depends on iodine for its hormones.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Thyroid gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The adrenal gland is composed of two types of tissues. Which of the following correctly describes their arrangement?

options.text: The adrenal medulla is centrally located and the adrenal cortex lies outside it
The adrenal cortex is centrally located and the adrenal medulla lies outside it
The adrenal medulla and adrenal cortex lie side by side as two lobes joined by an isthmus
The adrenal medulla forms the outermost layer, the zona glomerulosa

solution.explanation: The centrally located tissue of the adrenal gland is the adrenal medulla; the adrenal cortex lies outside it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The cortex surrounds the medulla, not the reverse; an isthmus joins the two lobes of the thyroid; the zona glomerulosa is the outer layer of the cortex, not the medulla.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: The adrenal medulla is centrally located and the adrenal cortex lies outside it

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors. These receptors are located:

options.text: In every cell of the body
Only in the endocrine gland that secretes the hormone
Only in the blood plasma, which carries the hormone

solution.explanation: NCERT states that hormones produce their effects by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors, which are located in the target tissues only.
steps: They are present in the target tissues only
solution.why_others_wrong: If every cell had the receptor, every cell would be a target; the secreting gland and the blood carry the hormone but are not where its receptors lie.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: In the target tissues only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, can result in a condition called acromegaly. This condition is characterised by:

options.text: Excessive loss of water in urine and dehydration
Severe disfigurement, especially of the face

solution.explanation: Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called acromegaly. It may lead to serious complications and premature death if unchecked.
steps: Severe disfigurement, especially of the face = acromegaly
solution.why_others_wrong: Stunted growth is pituitary dwarfism (low GH); protruding eyeballs and weight loss describe exophthalmic goitre; excessive water loss describes diabetes insipidus (ADH problem).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: Severe disfigurement, especially of the face

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (action).

List-I:
A. Vasopressin
B. FSH (in females)
C. LH (in females)
D. TSH

List-II:
I. Stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles
II. Stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules of the kidney
III. Stimulates synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland
IV. Induces ovulation of fully mature (Graafian) follicles and maintains the corpus luteum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules (hence ADH). In females, FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles, while LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles and maintains the corpus luteum. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping FSH and LH ignores that FSH grows follicles while LH triggers ovulation; vasopressin acts on the kidney, not the thyroid, and TSH acts on the thyroid, not the kidney.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about parathyroid hormone (PTH) are correct?

(a) PTH acts on bones and stimulates bone resorption (dissolution/demineralisation).
(b) PTH stimulates the reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules.
(c) PTH increases the absorption of Ca²⁺ from the digested food.
(d) The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating level of TSH.
(e) PTH is a steroid hormone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PTH is a peptide hormone that raises blood Ca²⁺: it stimulates bone resorption, reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules and Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food. Its secretion is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions, not by TSH.
steps: (d) False: regulated by blood Ca²⁺ level
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (d) or (e) is wrong: PTH secretion follows blood calcium, and PTH is a peptide, not a steroid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Parathyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Besides regulating the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, melatonin from the pineal gland also influences:

(a) Metabolism
(b) Pigmentation
(c) The menstrual cycle
(d) Our defence capability
(e) The level of calcium in the blood

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: melatonin regulates the diurnal rhythm and also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and our defence capability. Blood calcium is regulated by PTH and thyrocalcitonin, not melatonin.
steps: (e) is the job of PTH and TCT
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (e) wrongly add calcium regulation; '(c) and (d) only' leaves out metabolism and pigmentation, which NCERT lists.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pineal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cancer of the thyroid gland or development of nodules in it may lead to hyperthyroidism, which adversely affects the body physiology.
Reason (R): Hyperthyroidism is caused by a deficiency of iodine in the diet.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cancer of the thyroid gland or development of thyroid nodules may lead to abnormally high levels of thyroid hormone synthesis (hyperthyroidism), which adversely affects body physiology. Iodine deficiency instead causes hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid (goitre).
steps: R: false - iodine deficiency gives hypothyroidism/goitre
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options A and B are wrong; A is an NCERT statement, so D is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman suffers from untreated hypothyroidism. Which set of features is the developing baby most likely to show?

options.text: Protruding eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate and weight loss
Stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism
Excessive urination and thirst due to impaired ADH release

solution.explanation: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective development and maturation of the growing baby, leading to stunted growth (cretinism), mental retardation, low intelligence quotient, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism.
steps: Maternal hypothyroidism -> defective development of the baby
Features: stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism
solution.why_others_wrong: Protruding eyeballs with high BMR is hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease); gigantism comes from excess GH; excessive urination from ADH deficiency is diabetes insipidus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones, commonly called corticoids.
Statement II: The corticoids that are involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called mineralocorticoids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The adrenal cortex secretes corticoids. Those involved in carbohydrate metabolism are glucocorticoids (e.g. cortisol); those that regulate the balance of water and electrolytes are mineralocorticoids (e.g. aldosterone).
steps: Statement II: false - carbohydrate metabolism = glucocorticoids
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II swaps the two classes of corticoids, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is the NCERT definition, so it is not false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Besides producing ova, the ovary also functions as an endocrine gland.
Reason (R): The ovary produces two groups of steroid hormones called estrogen and progesterone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The ovary is the primary female sex organ that produces one ovum in each menstrual cycle. It is also an endocrine gland because it produces two groups of steroid hormones, estrogen and progesterone.
steps: Secreting hormones is what makes the ovary an endocrine gland, so R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives exactly why the ovary counts as an endocrine gland, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Gonads
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (action).

List-I:
A. Estrogens
B. Glucagon
C. Adrenaline and noradrenaline
D. Progesterone

List-II:
I. Supports pregnancy
II. Increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs) and sweating
III. Stimulate the growth and activities of the female secondary sex organs
IV. Acts mainly on hepatocytes and stimulates glycogenolysis, raising the blood sugar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Actions of hormones of the adrenal, pancreas and gonads
solution.explanation: Estrogens stimulate the growth and activities of female secondary sex organs; glucagon acts mainly on liver cells and stimulates glycogenolysis, causing hyperglycemia; catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating; progesterone supports pregnancy.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping estrogens and progesterone confuses the follicle hormone with the pregnancy-supporting hormone; glucagon acts on hepatocytes, while piloerection and pupillary dilation are emergency effects of catecholamines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland; Pancreas; Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pituitary gland are correct?

(a) The pars distalis region is commonly called the anterior pituitary.
(b) The neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) is also known as the posterior pituitary.
(c) The pars distalis produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
(d) Oxytocin is produced by the pars distalis.
(e) Growth hormone is stored in and released from the neurohypophysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Regions of the pituitary and their hormones
solution.explanation: The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, prolactin, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH. The neurohypophysis (pars nervosa, posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are synthesised by the hypothalamus. GH is an anterior pituitary hormone.
steps: (d) False: oxytocin is made by the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary
(e) False: the neurohypophysis stores oxytocin and vasopressin, not GH
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) puts oxytocin in the wrong lobe and (e) puts GH in the wrong lobe, so every option containing either is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about hormonal disorders are correct?

(a) Acromegaly is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features become noticeable.
(b) In adult women, hypothyroidism may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
(c) Diabetes insipidus results from a deficiency of insulin.
(d) Patients with diabetes mellitus are successfully treated with insulin therapy.
(e) A low level of ADH increases water reabsorption by the kidney, so very little urine is formed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Acromegaly is hard to diagnose early and often goes undetected for years. Hypothyroidism in adult women may make the menstrual cycle irregular. Diabetes insipidus is due to impaired synthesis or release of ADH, which causes excessive loss of water (diuresis), not water retention. Diabetes mellitus (insulin-related) is successfully treated with insulin therapy.
steps: (e) False: low ADH reduces water reabsorption and causes diuresis
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) mixes up diabetes insipidus (ADH) with diabetes mellitus (insulin); (e) reverses the effect of low ADH; every other option includes one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland; The thyroid gland; Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In males, LH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.
Statement II: Growth hormone is secreted by the pars intermedia of the pituitary.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In males, FSH (not LH) and androgens regulate spermatogenesis; LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens. Growth hormone is secreted by the pars distalis; the pars intermedia secretes only MSH.
steps: Statement I: false - FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis
Statement II: false - GH is from the pars distalis
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements carry a swapped name (LH for FSH, pars intermedia for pars distalis), so any option calling either true is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the gonads are correct?

(a) The ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues.
(b) Progesterone is the hormone secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles before ovulation.
(c) After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted into the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone.
(d) The testis performs dual functions, as a primary sex organ and as an endocrine gland.
(e) The Leydig cells are located inside the seminiferous tubules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Testis and ovary as endocrine glands
solution.explanation: The ovary has ovarian follicles and stromal tissues; growing follicles secrete estrogen, and after ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone. The testis is both a primary sex organ and an endocrine gland; it has seminiferous tubules and stromal (interstitial) tissue, and the Leydig cells lie in the intertubular spaces.
steps: (e) False: Leydig cells are in the intertubular (interstitial) spaces
solution.why_others_wrong: (b) gives the growing follicles the corpus luteum's hormone; (e) puts the Leydig cells inside the tubules; every other option contains one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In human males, the seminal plasma together with the sperms constitutes the:

solution.explanation: The secretions of the male accessory glands form the seminal plasma. The seminal plasma along with the sperms constitutes the semen.
solution.why_others_wrong: Colostrum is the early milk of lactation; amniotic fluid surrounds the foetus; the antrum is the fluid-filled cavity of the tertiary follicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Semen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Each human testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm. Its width is about:

solution.explanation: NCERT: each testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm and a width of about 2 to 3 cm.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10-12 cm is the length of an oviduct; the width cannot exceed the 4-5 cm length; 0.2-0.3 cm is far too small.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option A: 2 to 3 cm

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules. This release is called:

solution.explanation: Spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis. The sperm heads then become embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation.
steps: Release of sperms from the tubules = spermiation
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermiogenesis is the change of spermatids into sperms, which happens before release; insemination is the release of semen into the vagina; ovulation is the release of the ovum from the ovary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Spermiation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The mitotic divisions (cleavage) of the human zygote as it moves towards the uterus form 2, 4, 8 and 16 daughter cells. These daughter cells are called:

solution.explanation: Cleavage starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus and forms 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres.
steps: Cleavage = mitotic divisions of the zygote
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermatids come from meiosis in the testis; polar bodies come from the unequal meiotic divisions of the oocyte; granulosa cells surround the oocyte in the follicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Blastomeres

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The shape of the human uterus is like:

solution.explanation: The uterus is single and is also called the womb. Its shape is like an inverted pear, and it is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.
solution.why_others_wrong: The funnel with fimbriae is the infundibulum of the oviduct; a coiled tube describes the seminiferous tubule; the uterus has no bean-like shape.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option A: An inverted pear

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the secretions of which of the following are essential for the maturation and motility of sperms?

options.text: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate

solution.concept: Role of male accessory ducts and glands
solution.explanation: Sperms released from the seminiferous tubules are transported by the accessory ducts. The secretions of the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate are essential for the maturation and motility of sperms.
steps: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate
Their secretions -> maturation and motility of sperms
solution.why_others_wrong: Ovary, oviduct and uterus are female organs; Leydig cells secrete androgens into the blood, not secretions for sperm maturation; the urinary bladder and ureters belong to the excretory system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate

Statement II: The uterus is single and is also called the womb.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the structure of a human sperm are correct?

(a) A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of the sperm.
(b) The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus.
(c) The sperm is made up of a head, neck, middle piece and tail.
(d) The tail of the sperm contains numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for its movement.
(e) The acrosome covers the posterior portion of the sperm head.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A sperm is a microscopic structure made of a head, neck, middle piece and tail; a plasma membrane envelops the whole body. The head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like acrosome. The middle piece (not the tail) has numerous mitochondria that produce energy for the tail's movement.
steps: (d) False: mitochondria are in the middle piece
(e) False: the acrosome covers the anterior portion
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) moves the mitochondria to the tail and (e) moves the acrosome to the back of the head, so every option with either is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The endometrium of the uterus is maintained during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle.
Reason (R): The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the luteal phase the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone. Progesterone is essential for maintaining the endometrium, which is needed for implantation of a fertilised ovum.
steps: Progesterone from the corpus luteum is the reason the endometrium is maintained
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the cause of A, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of the normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause.
Statement II: The secretion of the gonadotropins (LH and FSH) decreases gradually during the follicular phase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cyclic menstruation indicates the normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause. During the follicular phase the secretion of gonadotropins increases gradually, stimulating follicular development and estrogen secretion by the growing follicles.
steps: Statement II: false - gonadotropins increase gradually in the follicular phase
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses the trend of LH and FSH, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (phase of the menstrual cycle) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Menstrual phase
B. Follicular phase
C. Ovulatory phase
D. Luteal phase

List-II:
I. Remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum
II. Breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels when the ovum is not fertilised
III. Primary follicles grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle
IV. Rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The menstrual phase is the breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels (when the ovum is not fertilised). In the follicular phase, primary follicles grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle. In the ovulatory phase, the Graafian follicle ruptures and releases the ovum. In the luteal phase, the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum.
solution.why_others_wrong: Follicle growth precedes and ovulation follows it, so swapping B and C is wrong; the corpus luteum forms after ovulation, not during menstruation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The mammary glands of a female differentiate during pregnancy. They start producing milk:

options.text: From the first month of pregnancy
Only from puberty onwards, in every menstrual cycle

solution.explanation: NCERT: the mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and start producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation.
steps: Milk production begins: towards the end of pregnancy
solution.why_others_wrong: Milk production does not start early in pregnancy or in non-pregnant cycles; the initial milk (colostrum) is already available in the first days after birth, so it does not begin weeks later.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Parturition and lactation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Towards the end of pregnancy

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens).
Reason (R): Androgens are synthesised and secreted by the Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens). Androgens are secreted by the Leydig (interstitial) cells in the intertubular spaces; the Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.
steps: R: false - androgens come from the Leydig cells
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options A and B are wrong; A is an NCERT statement, so D is wrong.

steps: Last, narrow part joining the uterus: isthmus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During fertilisation in humans, the secretions of the acrosome help the sperm to:

options.text: Block the entry of additional sperms into the ovum
Attach the blastocyst to the endometrium
Produce energy for the movement of the tail
Enter the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane

questions.subject: Zoology

Which of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are correct?

(b) The changes in the ovary and the uterus during the cycle are induced by changes in the levels of pituitary and ovarian hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The female gamete released from the Graafian follicle at ovulation is a secondary oocyte.
Reason (R): The primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle completes its first meiotic division before ovulation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows and completes its first meiotic division, an unequal division giving a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The Graafian follicle then ruptures and releases this secondary oocyte (ovum) by ovulation. The second meiotic division is completed only after a sperm enters.
steps: Because meiosis I is completed before ovulation (and meiosis II only after sperm entry), the released cell is a secondary oocyte: R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: The timing of meiosis I in R is exactly why the released gamete is a secondary oocyte, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (oogenesis)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

A. Primary follicle
B. Secondary follicle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a population, the genotype frequencies for a gene with two alleles, A and a, are AA = 0.45, Aa = 0.30 and aa = 0.25. What is the frequency of allele a in this population?

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution: features common to all vertebrate embryos but absent in adults, e.g. a row of vestigial gill slits behind the head in all vertebrate embryos including humans, which is functional only in fish. Karl Ernst von Baer disapproved this proposal, noting that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.
steps: Statement I: false - von Baer disapproved it; embryos never pass through adult stages of others
Statement II: false - vestigial gill slits are in embryos and absent in adult humans
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I reverses von Baer's finding and Statement II moves the gill slits from embryos to adults, so any option calling either true is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Evidences for evolution
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

The same would take millions of years in fish or fowl because their life spans are in years. The rate of appearance of new forms is linked to life cycle or life span.

Chance events in nature and chance mutation in the organisms
Changes that organisms make deliberately to meet their needs
A fixed plan in which every species was created as such

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the Hardy-Weinberg principle are correct?

(a) p² + 2pq + q² = 1 is a binomial expansion of (p + q)².
(b) When allele frequencies are stable, the gene pool (total genes and their alleles in a population) remains a constant; this is called genetic equilibrium.
(c) When the frequency measured differs from the expected values, the difference (direction) indicates the extent of evolutionary change.
(d) Natural selection does not change the allele frequencies of a population.
(e) Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is maintained even when gene migration occurs repeatedly.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: allele frequencies in a population are stable and constant from generation to generation; the gene pool remains a constant (genetic equilibrium). p² + 2pq + q² = 1 is the binomial expansion of (p + q)². A difference between measured and expected frequencies indicates the extent of evolutionary change. Gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, recombination and natural selection all disturb the equilibrium.
steps: (d) False: natural selection changes allele frequencies
(e) False: gene flow disturbs the equilibrium
solution.why_others_wrong: Natural selection and gene flow are two of the five factors that disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, so any option with (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A rare autosomal recessive disorder affects 1 in every 10,000 individuals of a population that is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Approximately what proportion of the population are heterozygous carriers?

solution.concept: Carrier frequency of a rare recessive allele
solution.explanation: Affected individuals are aa, so q² = 1/10,000 and q = 0.01; p = 0.99. Carriers are heterozygotes, 2pq = 2 × 0.99 × 0.01 = 0.0198, i.e. about 2%, or about 1 in 50.
solution.shortcut: For a rare allele p ≈ 1, so carriers ≈ 2q = 2 × 0.01 = 0.02.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 in 100 is q, the allele frequency, not the carrier frequency; 1 in 10,000 is q², the affected frequency; 1 in 5,000 is 2q², which wrongly doubles the affected frequency.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg principle
solution.final_answer: Option B: About 1 in 50 (about 2%)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (agent or technique) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. X-rays and gamma rays
B. Tobacco smoke
C. Oncogenic viruses
D. Radiography

List-II:
I. Contains chemical carcinogens identified as a major cause of lung cancer
II. Diagnostic technique that uses X-rays
III. Ionising radiations that cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation
IV. Carry genes called viral oncogenes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ionising radiations like X-rays and gamma rays cause DNA damage leading to neoplastic transformation. Chemical carcinogens in tobacco smoke are a major cause of lung cancer. Cancer-causing (oncogenic) viruses have genes called viral oncogenes. Radiography, which uses X-rays, is one of the techniques to detect cancers of internal organs.
solution.why_others_wrong: X-rays as such are carcinogenic radiations, while radiography is the diagnostic use of X-rays; swapping these, or swapping the chemical carcinogen (tobacco) with the biological one (viruses), gives a wrong code.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Cancer (causes and detection)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the term AIDS, 'acquired' indicates that the immune deficiency is acquired during the lifetime of an individual and is not a congenital disease.
Statement II: In the term AIDS, 'syndrome' refers to a single specific symptom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome: a deficiency of the immune system acquired during the lifetime of an individual, indicating that it is not a congenital disease. 'Syndrome' means a group of symptoms.
steps: Statement II: false - syndrome means a group of symptoms
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Syndrome' is a group of symptoms, so options calling Statement II true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's explanation of 'acquired', so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', AIDS
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a measure that NCERT suggests for the prevention and control of drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents?

options.text: Education and counselling to face problems and stresses
Seeking help from parents and peers
Pushing the child to perform beyond his/her threshold limits in studies or sports
Seeking help from psychologists, psychiatrists and de-addiction and rehabilitation programmes

solution.concept: Prevention and control of drug/alcohol abuse
solution.explanation: NCERT's measures: avoid undue peer pressure (a child should not be pushed unduly to perform beyond his/her threshold limits in studies, sports or other activities); education and counselling to face problems and stresses; seeking help from parents and peers; looking for danger signs; and seeking professional and medical help from psychologists, psychiatrists and de-addiction and rehabilitation programmes.
steps: Avoid undue peer pressure: do NOT push the child beyond threshold limits
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are NCERT's own recommended measures; pushing a child beyond his/her limits is exactly what NCERT says to avoid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Prevention and control (drugs and alcohol abuse)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Pushing the child to perform beyond his/her threshold limits in studies or sports

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Entamoeba histolytica, which causes amoebiasis, is a protozoan parasite of the human small intestine.
Statement II: Heat and moisture help ringworm fungi to grow, which makes them thrive in skin folds such as those in the groin or between the toes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite in the large intestine of humans and causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery). In ringworm, heat and moisture help the fungi grow, so they thrive in skin folds such as in the groin or between the toes.
steps: Statement I: false - large intestine, not small intestine
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I gives the wrong part of the intestine, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common diseases in humans
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The two core techniques that enabled the birth of modern biotechnology are:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the two core techniques are genetic engineering (altering the chemistry of genetic material to introduce it into host organisms and change their phenotype) and bioprocess engineering (maintenance of a sterile, microbial contamination-free ambience to grow only the desired microbe or eukaryotic cell in large quantities).
solution.why_others_wrong: Breeding and husbandry are traditional improvement methods; fermentation and pasteurisation are older processes; radiography and CT are diagnostic imaging techniques.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option B: Genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In 1963, two enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophage in Escherichia coli were isolated. One of them added methyl groups to DNA. The other:

options.text: Joined DNA fragments and was called DNA ligase
Copied RNA into DNA and was called reverse transcriptase
Removed RNA from DNA preparations and was called ribonuclease
Cut DNA and was called a restriction endonuclease

solution.explanation: NCERT: in 1963 the two enzymes responsible for restricting bacteriophage growth in E. coli were isolated. One added methyl groups to DNA, while the other cut DNA; the latter was called restriction endonuclease.
steps: Enzyme 1: adds methyl groups to DNA
solution.why_others_wrong: Ligase joins DNA; reverse transcriptase is the enzyme of retroviruses such as HIV; ribonuclease is used to remove RNA during DNA isolation. None of them restricts phage growth by cutting DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: Cut DNA and was called a restriction endonuclease

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In an agarose gel stained with ethidium bromide and exposed to UV light, the separated DNA fragments are seen as:

solution.explanation: DNA fragments can be visualised only after staining with ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation; they appear as bright orange coloured bands.
solution.why_others_wrong: Blue and white colonies describe recombinant selection with a chromogenic substrate, not bands on a gel; ethidium bromide-stained DNA glows orange, not green.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Separation and isolation of DNA fragments
solution.final_answer: Option A: Bright orange coloured bands

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), multiple copies of the gene or DNA of interest are synthesised in vitro using:

options.text: A restriction enzyme and DNA ligase
Two sets of primers and the enzyme DNA polymerase
Reverse transcriptase and a single primer

solution.explanation: In PCR, multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest are synthesised in vitro using two sets of primers (small chemically synthesised oligonucleotides complementary to regions of the DNA) and the enzyme DNA polymerase.
solution.why_others_wrong: Restriction enzyme and ligase cut and join DNA; reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA; lysozyme and ribonuclease are used during DNA isolation. None amplifies DNA by PCR.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option B: Two sets of primers and the enzyme DNA polymerase

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following lists antibiotics whose resistance genes are normally considered useful selectable markers for E. coli?

solution.explanation: NCERT: genes encoding resistance to antibiotics such as ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline or kanamycin are considered useful selectable markers for E. coli.
solution.why_others_wrong: Lysozyme, cellulase and chitinase are enzymes for breaking cells; ethidium bromide and agarose are used in gel electrophoresis; insulin and interferon are recombinant products, not antibiotics.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors (selectable marker)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline and kanamycin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Each restriction endonuclease functions by 'inspecting' the length of a DNA sequence.
Statement II: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of four base pairs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Each restriction endonuclease inspects the length of a DNA sequence, binds when it finds its recognition sequence and cuts both strands. Hind II always cuts DNA at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of six base pairs, called its recognition sequence.
steps: Statement II: false - six base pairs, not four
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT gives a six-base-pair recognition sequence for Hind II, so options calling Statement II true are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) are correct?

(a) By repeating the process, a DNA segment can be amplified approximately a billion times.
(b) The amplified fragment can be used to ligate with a vector for further cloning.
(c) Each cycle consists of denaturation, annealing and extension, in that order.
(d) PCR requires a living host cell to amplify DNA.
(e) In the extension step, DNA polymerase removes the primers from the template.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PCR is carried out in vitro. Each cycle has denaturation of double-stranded DNA, annealing of primers and extension of the primers by DNA polymerase using the nucleotides and the template. Repeated many times, the segment is amplified about a billion times, and the amplified fragment can be ligated with a vector for cloning.
steps: (e) False: DNA polymerase extends the primers
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) contradicts the in vitro nature of PCR and (e) reverses what polymerase does to primers; every other option includes one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During isolation of DNA, the preparation is treated with a protease.
Reason (R): In the cell, genes are located on long DNA molecules intertwined with proteins such as histones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: To isolate DNA, cells are broken open, releasing DNA with RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and lipids. Because DNA is intertwined with proteins such as histones, the proteins are removed by treatment with protease (and RNA by ribonuclease). Purified DNA is then precipitated by chilled ethanol.
steps: Proteins bound to DNA must be removed; that is why protease is used: R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the reason protease is needed, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology (isolation of DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Plasmid
B. Cloning
C. Recombinants
D. Insertional inactivation

List-II:
I. Making multiple identical copies of any template DNA
II. Loss of activity of a gene product, e.g. β-galactosidase, because foreign DNA is inserted within its coding sequence
III. Autonomously replicating, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA
IV. Transformed bacterial colonies that carry the vector with the foreign DNA insert

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Plasmids are autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA. Cloning means making multiple identical copies of any template DNA. Recombinants are the transformants (colonies) carrying the insert. Insertional inactivation is the loss of a gene's activity (such as that of β-galactosidase) when foreign DNA is inserted in its coding sequence.
solution.why_others_wrong: A plasmid is the circular extra-chromosomal DNA and cloning is the copying of DNA; recombinants are colonies with the insert, whereas insertional inactivation is the loss of a gene's activity. Other codes swap these.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology; Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: After separation and purification, a biotechnological product is formulated with suitable preservatives. If the product is a drug, the formulation must additionally undergo:

solution.explanation: Downstream processing includes separation and purification of the product and its formulation with suitable preservatives. Such a formulation has to undergo thorough clinical trials in the case of drugs, and strict quality control testing is required for each product.
solution.why_others_wrong: Insertional inactivation is a way of selecting recombinants; heat shock is used to transform bacteria; annealing is a step of PCR. None is a step after formulation of a drug.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Downstream processing
solution.final_answer: Option B: Thorough clinical trials

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Small volume cultures can yield appreciable quantities of products, so bioreactors are not required for large-scale production.
Statement II: In a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor, sterile air bubbles are sparged, which greatly increases the area for oxygen transfer.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: small volume cultures cannot yield appreciable quantities of products; large-scale production needs bioreactors in which large volumes (100-1000 litres) are processed. In a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor, sterile air bubbles are sparged, which increases the surface area for oxygen transfer.
steps: Statement I: false - small cultures cannot give appreciable yields
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I contradicts the very reason bioreactors were developed, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Obtaining the foreign gene product (bioreactors)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A thermostable DNA polymerase is used in PCR.
Reason (R): The enzyme must remain active during the high temperature used for denaturation of the double-stranded DNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In each PCR cycle the double-stranded DNA is denatured at high temperature. NCERT states that the thermostable DNA polymerase (isolated from Thermus aquaticus) is used because it remains active during this high temperature induced denaturation.
steps: Surviving the denaturation temperature is the reason a thermostable enzyme is chosen
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the reason for A, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A PCR is started with a single double-stranded DNA molecule. Each cycle doubles the DNA, and every new molecule is made of one old and one new strand. After 5 cycles, how many double-stranded molecules contain NO strand of the original template molecule?

solution.explanation: After n cycles there are 2^n molecules. The two original strands are never destroyed; each stays paired with a new strand, so exactly 2 molecules carry an original strand. The rest are made entirely of new strands.
solution.why_others_wrong: 32 is the total number of molecules; 31 assumes only one molecule keeps template DNA, but there are two template strands; 16 is the number after 4 cycles or half of 32.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option C: 30

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Foreign DNA is ligated at the BamHI site of pBR322, which lies within the tetracycline resistance gene, and the products are used to transform E. coli. On an ampicillin-containing medium, 200 colonies grow. When these 200 colonies are transferred to a tetracycline-containing medium, 150 of them grow. How many of the 200 colonies are recombinants?

solution.concept: Selection of recombinants by insertional inactivation
solution.explanation: All 200 colonies are transformants (they carry ampR). Insertion at the BamHI site inactivates tetR, so recombinants grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline. Non-recombinants grow on both. Recombinants = colonies that fail on tetracycline.
solution.why_others_wrong: 150 are the non-recombinants that kept tetracycline resistance; 200 counts all transformants; 350 adds the two counts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors (selectable marker; insertional inactivation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 50

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A circular plasmid with a single EcoRI site is cut with EcoRI, and a foreign DNA fragment with EcoRI sticky ends at both ends is inserted. How many phosphodiester bonds must DNA ligase form to give a covalently closed circular recombinant plasmid?

solution.concept: Action of DNA ligase on sticky ends
solution.explanation: A restriction enzyme cuts each of the two strands at specific points in the sugar-phosphate backbone. The insert joins the vector at two junctions, and at each junction both strands have a nick in the backbone that ligase must seal.
steps: Nicks per junction = 2 (one in each strand)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only the junctions and forgets that both strands are cut; 1 treats the insertion as a single join; 8 double-counts each nick.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes, ligase)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 4

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: 'Disarmed pathogen' vectors, when allowed to infect the cell, transfer the recombinant DNA into the host.
Statement II: Biolistics (gene gun) is a method suitable mainly for animal cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT lists micro-injection (DNA injected into the nucleus of an animal cell), biolistics or gene gun (suitable for plants; cells bombarded with gold or tungsten micro-particles coated with DNA) and disarmed pathogen vectors, which transfer the recombinant DNA into the host when allowed to infect the cell.
steps: Statement II: false - biolistics is the method suitable for plants
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT names biolistics as suitable for plants (micro-injection is the animal-cell method), so options calling Statement II true are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Insertion of recombinant DNA into the host cell/organism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of steps for isolating pure DNA from a bacterial or plant cell?

options.text: Precipitate DNA with chilled ethanol → lyse cells with enzymes → treat with ribonuclease and protease
Lyse cells with enzymes → treat with ribonuclease and protease → precipitate DNA with chilled ethanol
Treat with ribonuclease and protease → precipitate DNA with chilled ethanol → lyse cells with enzymes
Lyse cells with enzymes → precipitate DNA with chilled ethanol → digest the precipitate with DNase

solution.explanation: The cell is first broken open with enzymes (lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plant cells, chitinase for fungi). RNA is removed with ribonuclease and proteins with protease; other molecules are removed by appropriate treatments. Finally, chilled ethanol is added and purified DNA precipitates as fine threads.
solution.why_others_wrong: DNA cannot be precipitated before the cells are opened; RNA and protein cannot be removed before they are released; DNase would destroy the DNA being isolated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology (isolation of DNA)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Lyse cells with enzymes → treat with ribonuclease and protease → precipitate DNA with chilled ethanol

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In 'Bt cotton', the abbreviation Bt stands for:

solution.explanation: Bt toxin is produced by the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt for short). The gene for the toxin has been cloned from the bacterium and expressed in plants such as cotton.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bt is the name of the bacterium, not a technique; E. coli does not produce the Bt toxin; biolistics is a gene transfer method.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option A: Bacillus thuringiensis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Besides mice, which of the following groups of animals does NCERT list as having been made transgenic?

options.text: Only primates such as monkeys and apes
Only insects such as fruit flies and mosquitoes
Rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish
No other animal; only plants besides mice

solution.explanation: NCERT: although transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been produced, over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
steps: Listed: rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT's list is rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish; it does not limit transgenic animals to primates, insects or mice.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Transgenic animals
solution.final_answer: Option C: Rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: To make tobacco plants resistant to the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia by RNA interference, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plants using vectors derived from:

solution.concept: Vector used in RNAi for nematode resistance
solution.explanation: Using Agrobacterium vectors, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host (tobacco) plants. They produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells, forming dsRNA that initiated RNAi.
steps: Genes produce sense + anti-sense RNA -> dsRNA -> RNAi
solution.why_others_wrong: Disarmed retroviruses are used to deliver genes into animal cells; NCERT names Agrobacterium for this tobacco work; HIV is a human pathogen, not a plant vector.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Pest resistant plants (RNA interference)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Agrobacterium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Some strains of Bacillus thuringiensis produce proteins that kill lepidopterans. NCERT gives which of the following as examples of lepidopterans?

solution.explanation: Some strains of Bacillus thuringiensis produce proteins that kill certain insects such as lepidopterans (tobacco budworm, armyworm), coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes).
solution.why_others_wrong: Beetles are coleopterans; flies and mosquitoes are dipterans; nematodes are roundworms, not insects.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture (Bt cotton)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Tobacco budworm and armyworm

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT states that transgenic models exist for many human diseases. Which of the following is one of the diseases it names?

solution.concept: Transgenic models for the study of disease
solution.explanation: Transgenic animals are designed to increase our understanding of how genes contribute to the development of disease. NCERT: transgenic models exist for many human diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer's.
steps: Diseases named: cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis, Alzheimer's
solution.why_others_wrong: Common cold, ringworm and typhoid are infectious diseases caused by pathogens and are not among NCERT's examples of transgenic disease models.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Transgenic animals (study of disease)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Rheumatoid arthritis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Rosie, the first transgenic cow, was produced in 1997.
Statement II: The milk produced by Rosie was nutritionally a less balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in 1997, the first transgenic cow, Rosie, produced human protein-enriched milk (2.4 grams per litre). The milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin and was nutritionally a MORE balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk.
steps: Statement II: false - more balanced, not less
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses NCERT's comparison, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Transgenic animals (biological products)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about Bt toxins and Bt crops are correct?

(a) Coleopterans killed by some Bt toxins are beetles.
(b) Dipterans killed by some Bt toxins include flies and mosquitoes.
(c) Bt cotton still needs heavy insecticide spraying to control bollworms.
(d) The Bt toxin kills insects by dissolving their exoskeleton.
(e) The Bt toxin is an insecticidal protein.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis forms protein crystals containing a toxic insecticidal protein. Some strains kill lepidopterans, coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes). Once activated in the alkaline gut, the toxin binds the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing swelling and lysis; it does not dissolve the exoskeleton. Bt cotton gives resistance to insects without the need for insecticides.
steps: (d) False: it acts on midgut epithelial cells
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) denies the main advantage of Bt cotton and (d) gives the wrong site of action; every other option contains one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture (Bt cotton)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): RNA interference (RNAi) involves the silencing of a specific mRNA.
Reason (R): A complementary dsRNA molecule binds to the mRNA and prevents its translation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: RNAi involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA (silencing).
steps: Binding of the complementary dsRNA and blocking of translation is how the mRNA is silenced
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the mechanism that produces A, so B is wrong; both are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Pest resistant plants (RNA interference)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (use of transgenic animals) with List-II (NCERT example or advantage).

List-I:
A. Normal physiology and development
B. Study of disease
C. Chemical safety testing
D. Vaccine safety

List-II:
I. Results are obtained in less time
II. Mice used to test the polio vaccine could replace the use of monkeys
III. Altering the formation of insulin-like growth factor to learn its biological role
IV. Increasing our understanding of how genes contribute to the development of disease

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: To study normal physiology, genes that alter the formation of insulin-like growth factor are introduced and the biological effects studied. Disease models increase understanding of how genes contribute to disease. Toxicity testing with transgenic animals gives results in less time. Transgenic mice used to test the polio vaccine could, if reliable, replace the use of monkeys.
solution.why_others_wrong: The insulin-like growth factor work studies normal physiology, not disease; faster results belong to toxicity testing, while replacing monkeys belongs to vaccine safety; the other codes swap these.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Transgenic animals

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Meloidegyne incognitia is a nematode (roundworm) that infects the roots of tobacco plants; it is not an insect. steps: Statement I: false - it is a nematode
solution.why_others_wrong: Calling a nematode an insect makes Statement I false, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's outcome, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Pest resistant plants (RNA interference)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
